glink_edge.runtime_observation: The running Lineage kernel exposed active glink-native-modem interrupts during the read-only inspection. This verifies the Linux endpoint exists, not that it is safe for Microkit to claim.

word2 RX tail (local consumer-owned by Linux backend)

fifo_item_directions.479: AP TX FIFO; Linux allocates/reuses 16 KiB
fifo_item_directions.480: AP RX FIFO; acquired from remote SMEM

shared_smem.descriptor_semantics: The 32-byte descriptor contains shared head/tail indices for both directions; Linux mutates the indices while the remote modem may concurrently access them.
shared_smem.linux_initialization_side_effects: Even if SMEM items already exist, the Linux backend sets the RX tail and TX head indices to zero before starting GLINK. A Microkit implementation must not copy this reset behavior without a verified remote-side reset/coexistence contract.
shared_smem.linux_lifecycle_reference: Matched qcom glink_probe registers the modem SMEM edge after SUBSYS_AFTER_POWERUP and unregisters it after SUBSYS_AFTER_SHUTDOWN; qcom_glink_native_probe then resets AP-owned indices and sends VERSION. VERSION/ACK negotiates protocol features only and does not prove empty FIFOs or authorize resetting shared indices.
shared_smem.smem_directory_lookup: Matched qcom_smem_get resolves an item through the validated global TOC or host-private partition allocator; item addresses are not fixed offsets from the reservation base. It takes TCSR hardware spinlock 3 during metadata lookup. Atoll DTS marks SMEM no-map and binds the lock through syscon 0x01f40000.

tcsr_hwspinlock.operations: Write Apps owner ID 1 and read back to acquire; write zero to release. The matched driver retries with a timeout.
tcsr_hwspinlock.source: Matched LineageOS drivers/hwspinlock/qcom_hwspinlock.c and Atoll DTS.

shared_smem.read_only_probe_requirements: Before any native item lookup, define safe mapping/cache attributes and compatible hwspinlock access, and bounds-check SMEM header, partition table, and allocation metadata against the 2 MiB reservation. Lock acquisition/release coordinates metadata but does not quiesce GLINK FIFOs or establish permission to inspect live indices.
shared_smem.offline_smem_parser: platforms/sunfish/smem_model.py resolves synthetic v12 host-private uncached entries with bounded checks; tests/sunfish_smem_model_test.py supplies fabricated fixtures only. No device read or mapping is implemented.
shared_smem.prepared_directory_probe: smem-directory-probe.system maps this live-FDT reservation read-only and maps only TCSR lock 3 read/write for acquire/release. It validates directory metadata and reports offsets/sizes for GLINK items 478-480 plus SMP2P modem/AP items 435/428 without dereferencing any item payload. The expanded temporary boot found none of those five items in host 0:1.
shared_smem.microkit_lifecycle_gap: No modem SSR coordinator or modem reset/ready service is implemented for Microkit. Keep transport disabled until a boot-time peer-state and exclusive-ownership contract exists.
shared_smem.microkit_policy: Keep this range unavailable to ordinary PDs. Do not allocate/reinitialize SMEM items, change indices, ring the mailbox, or consume modem IRQs without an explicit boot-time coexistence contract and a single trusted transport broker.

glink_protocol.initial_handshake: GLINK version/features exchange, then named channel open/open-ack for IPCRTR, followed by receive-intent negotiation and data messages.

wire_details.offline_codec: platforms/sunfish/wlfw_protocol_model.py parses synthetic bounded records and ring snapshots only; it does not inspect or mutate live SMEM FIFO indices or ring the mailbox.

glink_protocol.source: Matched LineageOS drivers/rpmsg/qcom_glink_native.c and Atoll IPCRTR child configuration.

wlfw_control_transport.implementation_gate: Before native QMI, define ownership/coexistence for modem GLINK, SMEM, mailbox, and IRQ. The current offline QRTR/QMI codec and state-machine harness uses synthetic fixtures only and does not map or mutate device SMEM.

icnss.interrupt_semantics: Twelve raw PDC-parented interrupt tuples, CE0-CE11. Decode through the inherited controller hierarchy as specified below; do not infer Linux virtual IRQ numbers from these cells.

interrupt_irq_decode.source: Lineage kernel drivers/irqchip/qcom/pdc.c delegates PDC translation to its GIC parent; drivers/irqchip/qcom/pdc-sdmmagpie.c contains no PDC pin mapping for these resulting INTIDs. GIC DT SPI number n maps to hardware INTID n+32, which is the seL4 GIC IRQ number.
interrupt_irq_decode.microkit_grant_policy: Decoded IRQs are reserved for the future trusted WLAN domain only. No IRQ capability or WLAN domain exists in the current image. SMP2P crash notifications must be mediated by a separate trusted broker.

smp2p.semantics: The two child specifiers are SMP2P entry bit numbers, not hardware IRQs. Linux routes the modem SMP2P parent doorbell (GIC SPI 451, seL4 INTID 483) through shared memory, then fans WLAN entry bit changes out as nested IRQs.
smp2p.microkit_policy: Do not grant the shared modem SMP2P parent IRQ or its shared-memory transport directly to WLAN. A future trusted modem-IPC/SMP2P broker must own and validate the shared-memory entry and deliver only narrow WLAN notifications. Until that broker exists, treat crash indications as unavailable; firmware-start policy must remain fail-closed.

msa.ownership_policy: Keep the full fixed pool outside ordinary allocations. Do not transfer any segment until QMI bounds, SCM ABI, VMIDs, cache behavior, and rollback are independently verified.

running_driver_source_evidence.interpretation: The running kernel release has the pinned source commit prefix, and the pinned ICNSS source matches a separate local Android 13 audit copy byte-for-byte. This does not prove the exact ICNSS source or configuration compiled into the running kernel, so production power-profile minting remains disabled.

power.voltage_request_semantics: ICNSS calls regulator_set_voltage(min,max). At pinned commit 28f9290ae067d3e7857126eb6312720dbe9c7c80, atoll.dtsi declares 3.000-3.312 V ranges, but both captured DTBs omit these config properties; that commit's icnss.c therefore retains 3.312 V min/max defaults for these DTBs. The RPMh VRM rounds min_uv up to whole mV and checks it against max_uv. The running driver identity is unverified, so these are source-derived requests, not measured output voltages.
power.lineage_clock_enable_after_rails: cxo_ref_clk_pin (optional, no clock-names in captured DT)
power.regulator_provider: All five supplies resolve to qcom,rpmh-vrm-regulator nodes using the apps_rsc mailbox; the WLAN driver does not program PMIC registers directly.
power.rpmh_supply_inventory_scope: Exact direct -supply references to the five ICNSS RPMh resources in the captured runtime and kernel DTBs. The live regulator-class capture below has on-state user counts matching these direct DT clients and loses one user per ICNSS rail with Wi-Fi disabled. This cross-check does not expose client identities, direct RPMh API users outside the regulator framework, other regulator devices aggregated into the same resource, or the complete Apps RSC cache.

lineage_runtime_regulator_delta_capture.sample_method: Read state, microvolts, and num_users from /sys/class/regulator while Wi-Fi is enabled, disabled, then restored. No direct PMIC or RPMh writes were issued by the capture.
lineage_runtime_regulator_delta_capture.semantics_and_limits: microvolts is the regulator framework value, not a direct electrical measurement; num_users is an aggregate count and does not identify consumers. The transition supports a WLAN-correlated one-user delta on each ICNSS rail, but does not enumerate other non-DT RPMh clients or establish a complete per-client vote ledger. /sys/kernel/debug and regulator_summary were unavailable.

lineage_runtime_bluetooth_status_capture.semantics_and_limits: The Android framework reports ON while bt_power rfkill is soft-blocked, and no hci0 sysfs device is present. This read was not simultaneous with the regulator delta. It cannot attribute retained regulator users to Bluetooth or establish active Bluetooth hardware use.

rpmh_dynamic_client_source.disable_order: disable each regulator, then request minimum voltage 0 and load 0

rpmh_vote_semantics.aggregation: The regulator core first combines each regulator device's consumer requests and sums loads for mode selection; for each shared RPMh resource, the provider then max-aggregates valid registers across regulator devices associated with that exact resource, separately for active and sleep sets.
rpmh_vote_semantics.active_ack: Upward active requests wait for ACK; a voltage request may also wait when its new maximum is below the previously requested voltage.
rpmh_vote_semantics.native_write_gate: A trusted service must arbitrate all requesters and preserve their contributions; MMIO readback is not a per-client vote ledger.

rpmh_controller.microkit_policy: Shared Apps RSC/mailbox. It services global RPMh votes; never grant its registers or mailbox channel directly to WLAN. A trusted RPMh broker must preserve all existing clients and mediate rail votes.

power.native_power_failure_policy: Treat the Linux sequence as observation only. Native power service must track each successful enable, unwind in reverse order, surface rollback failures, and keep firmware disabled on ambiguous rail/clock state.
power.policy: No regulator, clock, PMIC, or generic SMC capability is granted to WLAN. A future narrow platform power service must own sequencing and rollback.

lineage_runtime_observation.scope: Confirms the live Linux DT binding and device-group attachment only. The separately recorded diagnostic route capture provides post-attach S2CR/CB state; neither record delegates SMMU control to seL4.

route_source_comparison.resolution: The apparent SID mismatch came from comparing the generic sm6150.dtsi with Sunfish. Lineage's Google Sunfish DVT1.0 overlay is based on qcom-base/sdmmagpie.dtb; sdmmagpie.dts includes sdmmagpie.dtsi, whose ICNSS node declares 0x240/0x1. The DVT overlay does not override ICNSS/iommus, and the live Android FDT confirms phandle 0x30 with SID/mask 0x240/0x1. The generic sm6150.dtsi value 0x1640/0x1 is not the Sunfish overlay base. The live IOMMU group confirms Linux attachment, not the S2CR/CB state or seL4 authority. A separate 2026-10-09 diagnostic-kernel readback records the post-attach ICNSS route at slot 13/CB6 and IPA WLAN SID 0x521 at slot 9/CB38; that Linux runtime state is distinct from the earlier ABL handoff and does not establish seL4 authority.

lineage_runtime_route_capture.device_state: Temporary fastboot boot of a diagnostic LineageOS kernel; no partition was flashed.

Linux dynamically programmed these routes; this capture does not establish state inherited by a Fastboot-booted seL4 image, authority to reproduce them, or ownership of a translated DMA context.

bootloader_route_import.scope_caveat: Pinned Linux HLOS handoff implementation only. It is not a stable API or an seL4 delegation contract. The separately captured post-attach runtime routes were dynamically programmed by Linux and are not the ABL handoff state.

linux_route_programming.scope_caveat: Pinned Sunfish Linux HLOS behavior only. It does not prove that a Fastboot-booted seL4 image receives the same Apps-SMMU MMIO mapping, EL access, clocks/power, secure permissions, or exclusive route/context-bank ownership.

source_derived_behavior.context_bank_software_storage: devm_kcalloc allocates zeroed arm_smmu_cb storage at driver initialization
source_derived_behavior.no_table_match_behavior: qsmmuv500_init_cb returns without assigning cb->actlr when the device group has no matching qcom,actlr entry

source_derived_behavior.fresh_context_actlr_scope: Only a newly zero-allocated software context-bank record with no matching qcom,actlr entry; Linux writes that stored zero during non-dynamic context setup
source_derived_behavior.scope_caveat: Zero describes fresh zeroed software storage only. The pinned path does not clear the stored ACTLR on context-bank destruction or reset it on reuse; qcom,skip-init also prevents inferring a global hardware reset. The ICNSS Linux route is S1 bypass. None of these facts establishes the phone's current translated-context ACTLR or a value safe for seL4 to install.
source_derived_behavior.microkit_policy: The source-derived fresh unmatched WLAN ACTLR is zero, but use it only for a separately proven fresh exclusive context. Live hardware and reused-context values remain unknown. Keep SMMU programming disabled until SMMU power/ownership, a complete live route snapshot, exclusive context/slot, owned tables/data, hardware readback, and fault-handler contract are validated.

sel4_smmu_support.intent: Pinned seL4/Microkit source and generated-config audit only. It grants no SMMU, MMIO, SID-route, context-bank, DMA, power, or firmware authority.

smmu_v2_driver.boot_initializer: plat_smmu_init calls smmu_config_prob, smmu_mapping_init, then smmu_dev_reset
smmu_v2_driver.reset_effect: Sets every stream route to context-bank type with default CB index 0, invalidates every stream-match entry, disables all context banks, clears their fault state, clears ACTLR.CPRE on each bank, invalidates SMMU TLBs, then enables the SMMU
smmu_v2_driver.mapping_assumptions: The mapping code says it was tested only on TX2, assumes a static kernel virtual mapping for SMMU register windows, and maps each context bank into that fixed window.

sunfish_port.reason: The generic option is TX2-only, hardcodes base 0x12000000, uses TX2-only static mapping assumptions, and its boot initializer rewrites all stream routes, invalidates stream-match entries, disables all context banks and changes global SMMU state; a non-clobbering Sunfish handoff is not implemented.

capdl_smmu_support.source_comment: In future supporting SMMU can be done by matching on the IommuDeviceIdentifier or creating a new function.

scratch_build.change: Temporary SDF copy changed only the apps_smmu map permission from r to rw; the linked probe source remains read-only.

raw_mmio_mapping_check.scope: Proves the Microkit/CapDL build can grant an AArch64 protection domain writable CPU mappings of this physical MMIO aperture through ordinary frame mappings. It is not an AArch64 SMMU IO-address-space API, does not test whether hardware accepts EL1 writes, and proves no exclusive hardware ownership, safe route selection, or DMA authority.

sel4_smmu_support.resolution: A generic seL4 Arm SMMUv2 capability API exists, but it is not enabled or platform-supported by this Sunfish build. The generic code hardcodes the TX2 base and mapping assumptions, rewrites all routes and context-bank state during init, published verified AArch64 configurations exclude SMMU, and Microkit 2.3.1 does not model AArch64 SMMU address spaces or CSpace delegation of SMMU control caps. A scratch Microkit/CapDL build confirms a different candidate path: a protection domain can receive writable CPU mappings of the Apps-SMMU MMIO aperture as ordinary frames. The new Rust snapshot module reads every implemented SMR/S2CR pair, derives route overlap and inactive-slot candidates, and retains the selected slot preimage. The executor requires this preimage, checks both live slot registers before the first write, and stays retryable on a pre-write mismatch; this code is not connected to a hardware writer and does not prove the capture remains fresh under exclusive ownership. None of this shows that hardware accepts EL1 writes, that seL4 owns the route table, or that any route can be changed safely. Keep the production executor closed until a Sunfish-specific owner gate proves access, a fresh complete route snapshot, live compare-before-write through the actual MMIO adapter, non-clobbering single-route programming, and fault containment.

They are explicitly classified as inactive Linux allocations; a future consumer must define an owned physical extent and allocator exclusion before it is enabled.

enablement_gate: WLAN firmware remains disabled. The observed ICNSS and IPA stream contexts use stage-1 bypass in the Linux configuration; the shared Apps SMMU must not be reused until a dedicated translated context and a negative DMA-fault test are demonstrated. The upstream Linux-firmware candidate has a Qualcomm Atheros binary license with use restricted to those chipsets and requires unmodified bytes plus license notice; its Sunfish compatibility is unproven. Google phone-specific firmware-use rights for NexatrodeOS remain unverified; do not package or load those proprietary blobs without explicit permission.
